name: Cholera & mosquito-borne
summary: WHO counts over 3,000 cholera deaths in 2026, nearly nine in ten in Africa; DR Congo, Sudan and Yemen hard hit
state: WHO said on 10 Nov that more than 3,000 people died of cholera from January to September 2026, nearly nine in ten in Africa (SCMP). ECDC's overview of 27 Oct lists DR Congo as worst affected and Yemen and Afghanistan among countries with most new deaths (ECDC), and WHO reported a surge in Yemen as conflict intensified (Al Jazeera, 13 Oct). Searches on 22 Nov found no sign of these outbreaks ending, so large high-mortality outbreaks in conflict zones keep the Alert.
for_you: Risk to travellers is low with safe water and food hygiene. Check NaTHNaC travel health advice before visiting affected countries; cholera vaccine is available for some travellers.
rubric_hit: Large outbreaks with high mortality in conflict zones (DR Congo, Sudan, Yemen) = Alert

sources.title: SCMP — Over 3,000 already dead from cholera this year, says WHO
Al Jazeera — Cholera cases surge in Yemen as conflict intensifies, WHO says

why: Climate-sensitive diseases — cholera, dengue, chikungunya, Oropouche, West Nile and yellow fever — are hitting record levels and reaching new regions.
drivers: Conflict, floods, heat, El Niño, water and sanitation, mosquito range expansion.

rubric.alert: Large outbreaks with high mortality in conflict zones, or a WHO grade 3 emergency.
rubric.watch: Record-level seasons, or local transmission in countries where the disease was not established (including Europe).
